Earlier reports indicated that Apple had cancelled the long-rumoured all-glass iPhone designed to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. According to a Bloomberg report, this redesign is still set to be applied to the Pro models next year. Here are the details.

Bloomberg says the redesign plan is still on track

Investment research firm Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating this morning, citing supply chain checks showing that Apple has cancelled the all-glass iPhone originally planned for next year to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary.

The latest Bloomberg report says Apple is "expected to launch iPhone Pro models with a new glass-like appearance next year," noting that "the front and back of the phone will be made of glass, with internal codenames V73 and V74 respectively. The glass material will extend to the sides of the device, connected in the middle by a metal frame."

However, the report also mentioned that the project has undergone several revisions since its original conception:

The report further directly refuted the report issued by Jefferies this morning, stating that "Apple's product roadmap has not changed."

Jefferies's claims

Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said this morning that, based on the firm's supply chain checks, the all-glass iPhone has been cancelled due to poor production yields.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple's push towards higher-priced iPhones, one reason being that memory costs are rising. He added that cancelling the plan could affect Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and profit margins of its Pro models.

As a result, Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating and lowered its target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66. Prior to this, Jefferies had already cut its target price from US$308.92 on July 31, after Apple reported its 2026 fiscal year third-quarter results and issued a dour guidance for the fourth quarter.
